response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.dealedge AS side, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), s AS (SELECT orderslink, side, avg_net_fee_rate, record_count, AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY side) AS side_avg FROM g) SELECT orderslink, side, avg_net_fee_rate, record_count, avg_net_fee_rate - side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM s WHERE avg_net_fee_rate > side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC, orderslink LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The record count is the number of fee records in each group (COUNT(*)), including records whose rebrate is null, even though those records contribute nothing to the average.
orders.recordvault is unique per order, so the join does not duplicate fee records.
Groups whose average net fee rate is null (every record has a null rebrate) are excluded from the side average and from the output.
